question: If an angle of a parallelogram is 27° less than four-fifth of its adjacent angle, then find the smallest angle of the parallelogram.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of **adjacent angles** in a **parallelogram** is always 180°.

Let the **adjacent angle** be x.

x + (4/5 × x − 27°) = 180°

9/5 × x = 207°

x = 115°

Smallest angle = 180° − 115° = 65°.

**∴ The correct answer is 65°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

One angle = 4/5 × (**adjacent angle**) − 27°

**Formula Used:**

In a **parallelogram**, the sum of any two **adjacent angles** is 180° (**supplementary angles**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2c0d73bda1a092c6cc30e5d4ef052efe9599c463f9467ec2115cb212d4941643.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the **adjacent angle** be A.

Let the other angle be B.

⇒ B = (4/5)A − 27

⇒ A + B = 180 (Sum of **adjacent angles**)

⇒ A + (4/5)A − 27 = 180

⇒ (9/5)A = 180 + 27

⇒ (9/5)A = 207

⇒ A = (207 × 5) ÷ 9

⇒ A = 23 × 5 = 115°

⇒ B = 180° − 115° = 65°

Comparing 115° and 65°, the **smallest angle** is 65°.

**∴ The correct answer is 65°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Parallelogram

Opposite sides are **parallel** and **equal** in length. Opposite angles are **equal**, and **consecutive angles** are **supplementary** (sum to 180°).

Diagonals of a Parallelogram

The **diagonals** of a **parallelogram** bisect each other, meaning they cut each other into two equal parts at their point of intersection.

Area of a Parallelogram

The **area** is calculated as Base × Height, or using **trigonometry** as a × b × sin(θ), where a and b are adjacent sides and θ is the included angle.</p
